Verdicts.Verdict:
Reviewed against the approved spec by the authority. Review 0 findings; WriteEvidence scope audit 17 paths 0 findings; attempt-pair audit 2 pairs 0 findings; scope audit not-run on a clean tree, the honest F27 case. Verified independently: matchSimpleGlob returns zero hits in src/review/core.ts, suite 1442 pass 3 skip 0 fail, validate:ci exit 0.
DISCLOSURE 1, THE ROADMAP STEP WAS WRONG TWICE AND WAS CORRECTED BEFORE APPROVAL. Recorded as F79, fifth roadmap claim in this phase to fail construction. P2.2 prescribed scoping the lifecycle exclusion to exactly the reviewed bundle; shipped code already excludes any canonical C-* deliberately - isCliLifecyclePath carries the comment not keyed on the reviewed change id, pinned by a test named cross-bundle fold of A does not error a review of B - so a reviewed-id gate would have re-opened F11.2. P2.1's direction constraint claimed the dedup can only widen what review accepts; measured false for the query operator, which the two copies implement differently in both directions, so the sets are incomparable rather than nested. The practical claim survives only because no approved plan has ever used it. Both step texts were amended in the roadmap.
DISCLOSURE 2, THE AUTHORITY'S PLAN BRIEF WAS WRONG TWICE AND THE EXECUTOR FOLLOWED THE SPEC. It listed AC-LIFECYCLE-BOUND among the reddened criteria and then asserted its red came from the stay-audited half. Verified: isCliLifecyclePath returns false for anything outside the changes directory, so graph, verification and context already raise - both halves green at HEAD, which is why the approved spec had already exempted the whole criterion under F45. No red was manufactured. The brief also said to transcribe every pin into ObservedWriteScope; that reading would have authorized writes the spec forbids, and the executor's split - forced writes listed, unmoved pins held by non-edit - is correct.
DISCLOSURE 3, THE EXECUTOR DISCLOSED A LIMIT IN ITS OWN EVIDENCE, RECORDED AS F80. The zero-depth red bundled the porcelain and WriteEvidence audits into one case; the first expectation aborted, so the recorded red evidences the porcelain behaviour and never reached the WriteEvidence assertion. Both are green after the change and F68 was satisfied between signatures, so nothing was violated - but that fail event proves one of the two behaviours it is cited for. One recorded red, one observable property, is the rule now in the ledger.
DISCLOSURE 4, A SECOND EVIDENCE LIMIT DISCLOSED. The characterization cases were added during the production trip, so they were not observed against pre-edit HEAD in that session. They characterize the surviving matcher's behaviour rather than proving the two copies previously disagreed; the disagreement evidence is the two audit-level reds, which were red at HEAD and are silent after.
DISCLOSURE 5, WHAT REMAINS UNPINNED AND IS NOT CLAIMED. finding.file separator form; stored File entries carrying dot-slash or backslash; 8.3 short names; realpath divergence; real filesystem case-folding, of which only a platform-conditioned branch is asserted. src/artifact/scope.ts production was deliberately not edited, so the File-entry form is unchanged by design and is a separate change. F73 stands: every gate here runs on one platform and local green is darwin - CI is the only observer of separator behaviour, and the previous path-touching bundle closed with zero findings and then failed Windows CI.
DISCLOSURE 6. The divergence is wider than F60 recorded. Beyond zero-depth globstar the copies also disagreed on mid-path zero directories, leading globstar, the bare directory, dot-slash collapse, backslash form and case. The roadmap's single pinned pair is necessary and not sufficient; the plan pinned the wider set on the surviving export.
DISCLOSURE 7. decisions.md was written during the open window - F79 before execution, F80 mid-window - each in its own commit ahead of the implementation commit. It is outside every bundle's ObservedWriteScope by design, and the scope audit reads working-tree porcelain, so committing removed those edits from the audit's view rather than clearing them.
DISCLOSURE 8. The release note required by the roadmap is in the implementation commit body per D5.5, not in CHANGELOG.md, which is generated. AC-NO-GLOB-RULE survives as a describe name that no longer means what it says: it still forbids a registered glob shape and the undocumented pairs, but this bundle documents the globstar rule it was named against. Naming fossil, not a behaviour change.
